title: Termination Date for Early Termination Fees: Small Business Electricity Supply Terms and Conditions
content:
**Definition.** For the early termination fee on a Small Business Electricity Supply agreement, the termination date is fixed by the termination anchor. When the cancellation was made because the business closed and a drop effective date is on record, the termination date is that drop effective date, the day supply actually ends; when no cancellation request is on record and the agreement carries a close date, as after a switch-away or a final bill, the termination date is that close date; in every other case the termination date is the date the business confirmed the cancellation. The remaining months of the fee are counted from this termination date to the contract end date.

## Anchor by the agreement record

| Drop reason on the cancellation | Drop effective date on record | Drop requested date on record | Close date on record | Termination date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| business closed | yes | yes | any | the drop effective date |
| any other reason | yes | yes | any | the drop requested date (the date the business confirmed the cancellation) |
| none (no cancellation request) | no | no | yes | the close date |

## Hypothetical cases

- A florist cancels on 3 May with the drop reason business closed; the drop effective date is the next scheduled meter read, 21 May. The termination date is 21 May.
- A bakery cancels on 3 May to move to a cheaper offer; the drop effective date is 21 May. The termination date is 3 May.
- No cancellation was ever requested; the utility ended supply because another supplier enrolled the site, with a close date of 14 June. The termination date is 14 June.

## Remaining months from the anchor

Contract end date 31 December. From a termination date of 21 May the remaining months are 7, plus one because 31 is later than 21: 8. From 3 May they are 7, plus one: 8. From 14 June they are 6, plus one: 7.
